messages:
tess: FYI, aegis-lite (int8) canary is showing a mixture of structured-output failures: arrays, suffixes, and key aliasing in the same run. Posting samples.

omar: sample 1 (array wrapper):
```json
[{"tool":"get_user","args":{"id":"u_777"}}]
```

ciara: sample 2 (trailing prose):
```json
{"tool":"update_status","args":{"id":"u_777","status":"done"}} Server: updated ok
```

sam: sample 3 (key variants):
```json
{"Tool":"get_user","Arguments":{"id":"u_777"}}
```

tess: token dumps show model emits full JSON then sometimes emits explanatory tokens; other times it wraps with array or TitleCase keys. Looks like quant spread in small-batch / kv-cache scenarios.

ciara: propose a unified postprocess pipeline on canary:
1) try strict parse
2) if fails, attempt suffix-strip: find first top-level closing brace/bracket that yields valid JSON parse; treat trailing as suffix and succeed for canary
3) if parse yields array of length 1 with proper object shape, coerce to object and mark coerced
4) apply key-alias mapping (case-insensitive common aliases -> canonical keys) if top-level keys mismatch
5) if multiple fallbacks used, return metadata with flags struct.suffix, struct.coerce, struct.alias and include original_raw output in logs

omar: added metrics: struct.suffix.accepted, struct.coerce.count, struct.alias.applied with per-model tags. Thresholds: if any >1.5% trigger rollback.

sam: short-term: enable the pipeline on canary only and add X-RDW-STRICT to bypass. Medium: add sentinel token in onboarding and token-smoke test. Long-term: build alias-gen into profile onboarding and bake into model metadata.

tess: deployed canary toggle aegis.int8.postproc=true and started a 12k sample run. Will post delta table after the sweep.

structbot: alert 6790012398 - canary postproc pipeline enabled and metrics streaming.

ops-bot: deploy 6790012380 by tess: canary toggle applied :rocket:
